reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about the oxidation behavior of AlTiCrZrNbTa coatings as a function of Al content, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support these premises. Without cited passages, there is no way to verify whether these claims are grounded in earlier results or accurately represented.
premises: Al addition around 10 at.% promotes a continuous, adherent composite oxide (Al2O3, TiO2, Cr2O3) on AlTiCrZrNbTa coatings
Al-free or low-Al coatings form fragmented oxides and exhibit accelerated oxidation
Excessively high Al (≥17 at.%) promotes deleterious intermetallic formation and oxide discontinuity
The composite oxide layer effectively suppresses oxygen diffusion and maintains coating integrity
The optimal Al range is 9–14 at.%, with ~10 at.% being most effective
